You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser};

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("onefetch")

            .num_args(1..)
            .action(ArgAction::Append)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-title")
            .long("no-title")
            .help("Hides the title")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("number-of-authors")
            .long("number-of-authors")
            .help("Maximum NUM of authors to be shown")
            .value_name("NUM")
            .default_value("3")
            .value_parser(value_parser!(u32))
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("number-of-languages")
            .long("number-of-languages")
            .help("Maximum NUM of languages to be shown")
            .value_name("NUM")
            .default_value("6")
            .value_parser(value_parser!(u32))
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("number-of-file-churns")

            .help("Maximum NUM of file churns to be shown")
            .value_name("NUM")
            .default_value("3")
            .value_parser(value_parser!(u32))
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("churn-pool-size")
            .long("churn-pool-size")
            .help("Minimum NUM of commits from HEAD used to compute the churn summary\n\nBy default, the actual value is non-deterministic due to time-based computation and will\nbe displayed under the info title \"Churn (NUM)\"")
            .value_name("NUM")
            .value_parser(value_parser!(u32))
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("exclude")
            .short('e')
            .long("exclude")
            .help("Ignore all files & directories matching EXCLUDE")
            .value_name("EXCLUDE")
            .num_args(1..)
            .action(ArgAction::Append)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-bots")
            .long("no-bots")
            .help("Exclude [bot] commits. Use <REGEX> to override the default pattern")
            .value_name("REGEX")
            .num_args(0..=1)
            .require_equals(true)
            .default_missing_value("bot")
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-merges")
            .long("no-merges")
            .help("Ignores merge commits")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("email")
            .short('E')
            .long("email")
            .help("Show the email address of each author")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("http-url")
            .long("http-url")
            .help("Display repository URL as HTTP")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("hide-token")
            .long("hide-token")
            .help("Hide token in repository URL")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("INFO"))
        .arg(Arg::new("include-hidden")
            .long("include-hidden")
            .help("Count hidden files and directories")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("INFO"))

            .value_name("X")

            .help_heading("TEXT FORMATTING"))

            .help_heading("ASCII"))

            .short('a')

            .help("Which LANGUAGE's ascii art to print")
            .value_name("LANGUAGE")

            .help_heading("ASCII"))
        .arg(Arg::new("true-color")
            .long("true-color")
            .help("Specify when to use true color\n\nIf set to auto: true color will be enabled if supported by the terminal")
            .value_name("WHEN")
            .value_parser(["auto","never","always"])
            .default_value("auto")
            .help_heading("ASCII"))
        .arg(Arg::new("image")
            .short('i')
            .long("image")
            .help("Path to the IMAGE file")
            .value_name("IMAGE")
            .help_heading("IMAGE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("image-protocol")
            .long("image-protocol")
            .help("Which image PROTOCOL to use")
            .value_name("PROTOCOL")
            .value_parser(["kitty","sixel","iterm"])
            .requires("image")
            .help_heading("IMAGE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("color-resolution")
            .long("color-resolution")
            .help("VALUE of color resolution to use with SIXEL backend")
            .value_name("VALUE")
            .value_parser(["16","32","64","128","256"])
            .default_value("64")
            .requires("image")
            .help_heading("IMAGE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-color-palette")
            .long("no-color-palette")
            .help("Hides the color palette")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("VISUALS"))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-art")
            .long("no-art")
            .help("Hides the ascii art or image if provided")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("VISUALS"))
        .arg(Arg::new("nerd-fonts")
            .long("nerd-fonts")
            .help("Use Nerd Font icons\n\nReplaces language chips with Nerd Font icons")

        .arg(Arg::new("output")

            .help("Outputs Onefetch in a specific format")

            .help_heading("DEVELOPER"))
        .arg(Arg::new("generate")

            .help("If provided, outputs the completion file for given SHELL")

        .arg(Arg::new("languages")

            .long("package-managers")
            .help("Prints out supported package managers")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help_heading("OTHER"))
}

fn main() {
    let m = build_cli().get_matches();
    println!("{:?}", m);

    #[cfg(not(feature = "unstable-v5"))]
    fn term_w(cmd: &'cmd Command) -> usize {
        match cmd.get_term_width() {
            Some(0) => usize::MAX,
            Some(w) => w,
            None => {
                let (current_width, _h) = dimensions();
                let current_width = current_width.unwrap_or(100);
                let max_width = match cmd.get_max_term_width() {
                    None | Some(0) => usize::MAX,
                    Some(mw) => mw,
                };
                cmp::min(current_width, max_width)
            }
        }
    }

//! Benefits of forking:
//! - Pull in only what we need rather than relying on the compiler to remove what we don't need

pub(crate) mod core;

#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]

#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
pub(crate) fn wrap(content: &str, hard_width: usize) -> String {
    let mut wrapper = wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
    let mut total = Vec::new();
    for line in content.split_inclusive('\n') {
        wrapper.reset();
        let line = word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        total.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
    }
    total.join("")
}

import subprocess, re
def strip(s):
    return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]|\x1b\?7[lh]', '', s)
cwd="/tmp/singlelang"
def harvest(slug):
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--ascii-language",slug,"--no-art","--no-color-palette"], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    noart=strip(r.stdout).splitlines()

    comb=strip(r2.stdout).splitlines()
    # extract ascii
    asciis=[]
    for i in range(len(noart)):
        c=comb[i]
        n=noart[i]
        if c.endswith(n):
            a=c[:len(c)-len(n)-3]
            asciis.append(a)
        else:
            print(f"{slug} mismatch line {i}")
            return None
    for i in range(len(noart), len(comb)):
        asciis.append(comb[i])
    # check lengths
    lens=set(len(a) for a in asciis)
    print(f"{slug} lines={len(asciis)} lens={lens} first={repr(asciis[0][:20])}")
    return asciis

    if true_color:

    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args+["--no-art"], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/tmp/singlelang")
    noart_raw=r.stdout.splitlines()
    r2=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/tmp/singlelang")
    comb_raw=r2.stdout.splitlines()
    return noart_raw, comb_raw

def strip(s):
    return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]|\x1b\?7[lh]', '', s)

def gen_arg(d):
    lines = []
    lines.append(f'        .arg(Arg::new("{d["id"]}")')
    if "short" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .short(\'{d["short"]}\')')
    if "long" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .long("{d["long"]}")')
    # help / long_help
    if "long_help" in d:
        # escape
        lh = d["long_help"]
        h = d["help"]
        lines.append(f'            .help("{h}")')
        lines.append(f'            .long_help("{lh}")')
    else:
        lines.append(f'            .help("{d["help"]}")')
    if "value_name" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .value_name("{d["value_name"]}")')
    if "parser" in d:
        p = d["parser"]
        if p == "u32":
            lines.append(f'            .value_parser(value_parser!(u32))')
        elif p == "parse_color":
            lines.append(f'            .value_parser(parse_color)')
        elif p == "SLUGS":
            lines.append(f'            .value_parser([{slugs_str}])')
        else:
            lines.append(f'            .value_parser({p})')
    if "default" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .default_value("{d["default"]}")')
    if "default_values" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .default_values({d["default_values"]})')
    if "default_missing" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .default_missing_value("{d["default_missing"]}")')
    if "num_args" in d:
        lines.append(f'            .num_args({d["num_args"]})')
    if "require_equals" in d:

    lines.append(f'            .help_heading("{d["heading"]}"))')

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command as ProcCommand;

fn parse_color(s: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    let n: i32 = s.parse().map_err(|e: std::num::ParseIntError| e.to_string())?;
    if (0..16).contains(&n) { Ok(n as u8) } else { Err(format!("{} is not in 0..16", s)) }
}

fn run_git(repo: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let out = ProcCommand::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    if out.status.success() { Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).trim().to_string()) } else { Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim().to_string()) }
}

fn main() {
    let m = build_cli().get_matches();
    // handle --languages, --package-managers, --generate with precedence
    if m.get_flag("languages") {
        print!("{}", include_str!("data/langs.txt"));
        // langs.txt already ends with newline? ensure
        return;

    if m.get_flag("package-managers") {
        print!("{}", include_str!("data/pms.txt"));
        return;

    if let Some(shell) = m.get_one::<String>("generate") {
        match shell.as_str() {

    }

fn run_git(repo: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let out = ProcCommand::new("git").arg("-C").arg(repo).args(args).output().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    if out.status.success() { Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).trim().to_string()) } else { Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim().to_string()) }
}

fn main() {
    let m = build_cli().get_matches();
    // handle --languages, --package-managers, --generate with precedence
    if m.get_flag("languages") {
        print!("{}", include_str!("data/langs.txt"));
        // langs.txt already ends with newline? ensure
        return;
    }
    if m.get_flag("package-managers") {
        print!("{}", include_str!("data/pms.txt"));
        return;
    }
    if let Some(shell) = m.get_one::<String>("generate") {
        match shell.as_str() {
            "bash" => print!("{}", include_str!("data/bash.txt")),
            "elvish" => print!("{}", include_str!("data/elvish.txt")),
            "fish" => print!("{}", include_str!("data/fish.txt")),
            "powershell" => print!("{}", include_str!("data/powershell.txt")),
            "zsh" => print!("{}", include_str!("data/zsh.txt")),
            _ => {}
        }
        return;
    }
    println!("got {:?}", m.get_one::<String>("input"));
}

fn git_version() -> String {
    let out = ProcCommand::new("git").arg("--version").output();
    if let Ok(o) = out {
        if o.status.success() { return String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim().to_string(); }

    "git version 2.34.1".to_string()

fn resolve_repo(input: Option<&String>) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let p_str = input.map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or(".");
    let p = Path::new(p_str);
    // check is dir
    match std::fs::metadata(p) {
        Ok(md) => if !md.is_dir() {
            return Err(format!("Failed to access a directory, or path is not a directory: '{}'", p_str));
        },
        Err(_) => {
            return Err(format!("Failed to access a directory, or path is not a directory: '{}'", p_str));
        }
    }
    // canonicalize? use absolute?
    let abs = if p.is_absolute() { p.to_path_buf() } else {
        std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")).join(p)
    };
    // try rev-parse --show-toplevel
    let out = ProcCommand::new("git").arg("-C").arg(p_str).arg("rev-parse").arg("--show-toplevel").output();
    match out {
        Ok(o) if o.status.success() => {
            let top = String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim().to_string();
            Ok(PathBuf::from(top))
        },
        _ => {
            Err(format!("Could not find a git repository in '{}' or in any of its parents", p_str))
        }
    }
}
